- Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the first 10–15 days of the forecast horizon.
- Forecast shows gradual upward trend, but true prices often spike higher in the middle to late period (e.g., 75–80+), suggesting model fails to capture short-term volatility or policy-driven surges.
- Model overreacts to recent low prices (e.g., 68–70 range) by forecasting further downward, but true prices often rebound or show mean reversion toward higher levels.
- After a sharp spike in true prices (e.g., 80+), model forecasts remain flat or slightly increasing, missing the peak and failing to anticipate subsequent decline.
- Model exhibits lag in recognizing true price peaks — often forecasts peak too early or too late, leading to underestimation or overshoot.
- Model tends to ignore recent high prices in history when forecasting, leading to persistent downward bias.
- Model does not adjust for seasonality or policy-driven price shocks (e.g., auction results, cap changes) — forecasts remain linear or slowly increasing despite sharp true price movements.
- Model underestimates the impact of recent high prices on future prices — fails to show mean reversion or momentum correction.
- Model overestimates the persistence of low prices — forecasts remain low even after true prices rebound.
- Model fails to capture the “rebound effect” after a sharp drop — often forecasts a continued decline when true prices recover quickly.
